content:
maria: quick question — we're finalizing the "who changed what/when" event contract for the console and exports. main constraints: compliance teams want stable fields for audits, product wants compact rows for csv, infra wants minimal perf impact. how do we balance?

jason: +1. propose a small canonical shape that covers identity, resource, action, and delta. everything else can be optional metadata. example: 
```json
{
  \"event_id\": \"uuid\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2025-04-09T18:10:56Z\",
  \"actor_id\": \"user:maria\",
  \"actor_email\": \"maria@redwood.ai\",
  \"action\": \"update\",
  \"resource_type\": \"route\",
  \"resource_id\": \"routes/stripe-ingest\",
  \"before\": { /* optional compact snapshot or diff */ },
  \"after\": { /* optional compact snapshot or diff */ },
  \"tags\": [\"production\",\"dedicated\"],
  \"metadata\": {\"ip\": \"1.2.3.4\", \"deploy_id\": \"d-123\"}
}
```

devon: thinking about PII and retention: actor_email might need redaction for exports to external vendors. for internal console we can show full. suggest two derived views: canonical_event (full, internal only) + export_row (redacted, flattened). :lock:

katie: console UX notes: filters should map directly to event fields — actor, time range, resource_type, action, route/model tags. exports from UI should default to ndjson (stream-friendly) and offer a csv flattening for simple audits. also want a quick "who changed rollout" pivot that groups by rollout_id and shows before/after diff. :eyes:

sam: backend/infra constraints: event ingestion path is high-qps (billing and telemetry spikes). keep canonical event small (<1KB typical) and put heavy snapshots in an object store with a pointer. export API: support stream cursor + incremental export (start_ts/end_ts + cursor), and also ad-hoc S3 push for compliance teams. retention controls + legal hold flag.

jason: agree re: snapshot pointer. also add fields for provenance: rollout_id, rollout_stage, policy_id, route_version. quotas/changes need delta info like {\"quota_before\": 1000, \"quota_after\": 500}. that makes compliance queries straightforward.

maria: ui question — should we show the raw event JSON in console detail panel? product likes it for debugging but security wants to hide sensitive keys. maybe show raw but mask keys flagged as sensitive and allow a "reveal" action for authorized roles.

devon: +1. add a field `sensitivity_score` or `sensitive_keys` array so UI can auto-mask. and rely on access checks for reveal with audit trail (we should log who revealed).

katie: on export UX — add a checkbox "include snapshots (may be large)" with a size estimate. default off. also provide column mapping for csv so compliance can pick fields.

sam: about export performance — we'll implement ndjson streaming with backpressure and a server-side paginator. we should rate-limit exports per-org and surface estimated completion time for large ranges. also add an export job object so admin can retry/cancel.

jason: one more schema nit: canonical event should include `resource_path` like `orgs/123/routes/stripe-ingest` to make joins easier. and a `change_summary` short string for quick index.

maria: sounds good. next steps: write up the canonical schema draft, add export row shape and redaction rules, and mock the console export options. devon/sam/jason/katie — can you review by EOD tomorrow?

katie: I'll mock the UI checkboxes and CSV mapping screen — will post screenshots in this thread.

devon: I'll draft redaction policy + sample SQL for compliance queries.

sam: I'll sketch the export API (cursor semantics + s3 push) and job model; will capture performance numbers for 30d export.

jason: I'll assemble the schema doc and add field definitions and examples.

audit-bot: Export job 98765 completed for org 123 (ndjson, 95MB, 42k events) :white_check_mark: 

maria: perfect — thanks team. we'll iterate on the doc and merge into the eng-platform RFC repo.
